meta.title: Dev Workflow
meta.description: Development-workflow gatekeeper: skill-injected conventions, commit-message and doc-sync checks, guards for destructive git commands, and a gate on the actions other people can see.

command.toggle.description: Turn the development-workflow gatekeeper on or off.
command.toggle.hint: on | off | status | check [--message "type: subject"] | mark | unmark
command.toggle.unknown: Unknown subcommand "{input}". Use on, off, status, check, mark, or unmark.
command.toggle.mark.done: This repository is opted in: created {file}. The file is presence-only — its contents are never read, so it is safe to commit as-is.
command.toggle.unmark.done: This repository is opted out: removed {file}.
command.toggle.unmark.nothing: This repository was already opted out — no marker at {file}.
command.toggle.status.on: dev-workflow is on. Conventions stay resident as a short summary; details are read on demand.
command.toggle.status.off: dev-workflow is off. Nothing is injected and nothing is checked.
command.toggle.status.runtime_off: dev-workflow is off for this session — the configuration still says on. Type /dev-workflow on to bring it back.
command.toggle.on_done: Everything is registered again. The configuration file was not changed.
command.toggle.off_done: The tools, skill, triggers and guards are withdrawn. /dev-workflow stays available, so type /dev-workflow on to bring them back; the configuration file was not changed.
command.toggle.status.scope.all: Scope: every repository. This working directory is checked.
command.toggle.status.scope.marked.on: Scope: marked repositories only. This one is marked ({file}), so it is checked.
command.toggle.status.scope.marked.off: Scope: marked repositories only. This one is NOT marked, so nothing is checked here. Run /dev-workflow mark to opt it in ({file}).
command.toggle.status.never: No check has run in this session yet.
command.toggle.check.header: Development-workflow check of the working tree:
command.toggle.check.advised: Nothing blocks it, and {count} advisory note(s) were left: run /dev-workflow check to read them.
command.toggle.check.no_message: The commit-message rules were not part of this check: pass --message "type: subject" to include them.
command.toggle.check.message: The commit-message rules were judged against: {message}
command.guard.dangerous_warning: This command does something that cannot be undone: {pattern}.
command.guard.dangerous_warning.label: dangerous shell
command.guard.confirm_required: Check the target before approving. If it is not the one you meant, reject.
command.guard.denied: Run it deliberately outside the plugin, or relax `commandGuard.dangerousShell` in configuration.
tool.check_commit_message.description: Validate a commit message against Conventional Commits.
tool.check_commit_message.param.message: Full commit message: subject line, optional body, optional footer.
tool.check_commit_message.param.files: Repository-relative paths this commit touches. Used to note a commit that spans several modules.
tool.check_commit_message.error.empty: The commit message is empty. Write a subject such as `feat(parser): reject empty input`.
tool.check_commit_message.error.missing_: The commit message has no type prefix.
tool.check_commit_message.hint.format: Expected `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, for example `fix(git-guard): deny force push without confirmation`.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.breaking_: The `!` marker announces a breaking change, but no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer explains it. The header is valid on its own — add a line starting with `BREAKING CHANGE: ` to say what breaks and what to do instead.
tool.check_commit_message.error.changelo: A `feat` commit must add a `{changelog}` entry under `[Unreleased]`. Add one line saying what the feature does.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.subject_l: The subject is {length} characters; Conventional Commits asks for {max} or fewer. Move the detail into the body.
tool.check_commit_message.error.trailing: The subject ends with a period. Conventional Commits leaves it off.
tool.check_commit_message.error.empty_sc: The scope is empty: `feat(): x` names nothing. Either drop the parentheses or put the area in them: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`.
tool.check_commit_message.error.empty_su: The type and colon are there, but no subject follows: `fix(core):` says nothing. Write what changed after the colon.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.body_widt: A body line is {length} characters; the specification wraps at {max}. Wrap it so the message reads in a narrow terminal.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.multiple_: This commit spans several modules ({modules}). If those changes answer different questions, split them into separate commits.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.missing_s: This change touches only {module}; name it in the scope: `<type>({module}): <subject>`.
tool.check_commit_message.error.missing_: This repository requires a scope, but the subject has none. Name the area: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`.
tool.check_commit_message.ok: The commit message follows Conventional Commits.
tool.check_doc_sync.description: Check whether documentation was updated together with the code it describes.
tool.check_doc_sync.param.files: Repository-relative paths to check. Omit to read the working tree with `git status`.
tool.check_doc_sync.error.mirror: These files are kept in step with each other and only some of them changed. Changed: {changed}. Missing: {missing}.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.mirror_pending: A paired document is outside this change: {changed} is here, {missing} is staged or edited in the working tree. Finish the pair before the branch goes out.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.no_document: {count} code file(s) changed with no documentation update — for example {example}. Add or update a file under {docsDir} if the change is user-visible or architectural.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.changelog: {changelog} has no `[Unreleased]` entry for this change. Add one line saying what changed.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.readme_on_confi: This change edits {files}, which configure the whole project, and no file listed in `docs.readme` changed with it. Say what the configuration change means for a reader.
tool.check_doc_sync.ok: Documentation and code are in sync.
error.not_a_git_repository: This is not a git repository.
error.git_not_available: git was not found on PATH.
error.cancelled: The git command was cancelled before it finished.
security.guard.force_push: A force push rewrites remote history and can discard other people's commits.
security.guard.force_push.label: force push
security.guard.hard_reset: A hard reset discards uncommitted work permanently.
security.guard.hard_reset.label: hard reset
security.guard.clean_force: `{command}` deletes permanently, with no way back.
security.guard.clean_force.label: permanent delete
security.guard.branch_delete: `{command}` removes a ref; commits or tags that only it pointed at can go with it.
security.guard.branch_delete.label: delete a ref
security.guard.rebase.label: rebase
security.guard.amend: Amending a published commit rewrites shared history.
security.guard.amend.label: amend
security.guard.checkout_discard: `{command}` throws away work that was never committed.
security.guard.checkout_discard.label: discard work
security.guard.no_verify: --no-verify skips the hooks that protect this repository.
security.guard.no_verify.label: --no-verify
security.guard.outward_push: A push publishes this branch to the remote, where other people can see it.
security.guard.outward_push.label: push
security.guard.outward_tag: A tag is a public marker on a commit; other people start building against it.
security.guard.outward_tag.label: tag
security.guard.outward_pull_request: Opening a pull request asks other people to review this branch.
security.guard.outward_issue: Opening an issue files a public report against this repository, where other people will read it.
security.guard.outward_issue.label: open an issue
security.guard.outward_publish: Publishing a version is visible to everyone who installs the package, and cannot be taken back.
security.guard.outward_publish.label: publish
security.guard.suggest_force_with_lease: Prefer --force-with-lease: it refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.
security.guard.approval_rejected: This operation was not approved, so it stays refused.
security.guard.approval_cancelled: The approval question for this operation was cancelled, so it was refused.
security.guard.approval_unavailable: This operation needs approval, but no approval channel is available, so it was refused.
approval.disabled: Nobody was asked: this session's approval policy is "never", so approval is refused without a prompt. To let this through, switch to a permission preset that asks, or set this operation to "allow" — which stands until you set it back to "ask". The settings panel marks such a field as overridden, so you can find it again.
approval.disabled_trigger: Nobody was asked: this session's approval policy is "never", so approval is refused without a prompt. This gate judges a whole class of actions, so there is no per-operation setting to relax: either tune the rule in the settings panel, turn the check off with `enableOwnTrigger`, or perform the action outside this workflow.
security.sensitive_file_blocked: This call names a sensitive file, so it was not run: {file} (matched `{rule}`). Read the value from the environment, or ask the user to paste what is needed instead of the whole file.
security.sensitive_file_blocked.label: sensitive file
security.secret_detected: This call carries what looks like a live credential, so it was not run. The value was not logged and is not repeated here.
security.secret_detected.label: credential
security.secret_pattern_matched: Pattern matched: {pattern}. Rotate the credential if it has already been sent anywhere, and keep it in the environment or a secret store rather than in a prompt, a source file, or a command.
security.secret_search: This call carries what looks like a live credential, and it was allowed because the command only reads. A search cannot carry the value off the machine, and refusing it would only make the leak harder to find. The value was not logged and is not repeated here; if it is live, rotate it.
security.secret_search.label: credential search
audit.enabled: Security audit enabled. Guard decisions are appended to {path}, which stays out of the model's context. Whether git tracks it is up to this repository's .gitignore.
audit.disabled: Security audit disabled. Guard decisions are no longer recorded, so a reviewer has no trail after the session ends.
audit.not_ignored: The audit trail at {path} is not ignored by git, so the next commit would carry a record of every refused credential and every sensitive path this session touched. Add {path} to .gitignore, or point audit.path somewhere that is already ignored.
trigger.pre_commit.detected: Checking this commit against the project workflow rules.
trigger.pre_commit.reason:
This commit breaks the project workflow rules.
{details}
trigger.pre_commit.detail:
The commit check also found this:
{details}
trigger.pre_commit.settled_by: The other gate asked about this call first. Answering it answers this too.
trigger.pre_commit.warn.degraded: The changed-file check did not run, so the documentation rules were skipped: {reason}
trigger.pre_commit.warn.unreadable: The commit message is written by this command (`{source}`), so it could not be read before the call runs. The message rules were not applied — check the message yourself.
trigger.pre_pr.detected: Checking this pull request against the project workflow rules.
trigger.pre_pr.reason:
This pull request breaks the project workflow rules.
{details}
trigger.pre_pr.error.description: The pull request description is missing a section the template asks for: {sections}. Keep each section heading exactly as the template spells it; the text under them may be in any language.
trigger.pre_pr.error.verification: `## {section}` states no evidence: a reviewer has nothing to run. Give the command or the steps, and what a passing result looks like. Every other section may be answered with "none"; this one is the section that shows the change was actually run.
trigger.pre_pr.error.checklist: The pull request description leaves {count} checklist item(s) unticked. Tick each one, or delete the line if it does not apply.
trigger.pre_pr.error.empty: The pull request description is empty. Write what changed and why.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.issue: The pull request names no issue. Reference one (`Closes #12`) when an issue exists, so the change can be traced back to its reason.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.self_issue: The only issue reference in this pull request is the pull request itself. That traces the change back to nothing; reference the issue it comes from when there is one.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.filled: The title and description come from the commits (`--fill`, or an interactive prompt), so they could not be checked here. Under squash merge the filled title becomes the commit on the main branch — check it before merging.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.conflict: `{branch}` is still unmerged and would conflict with this branch on {files}. Each branch merges cleanly against the base on its own, so whichever lands second pays for the conflict — rebase this branch after the other one merges, or merge them in the other order.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.title_literal: The title is assembled by the shell (`$(...)`, a variable, or backticks), so only its literal text could be read. Check the resulting title yourself.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.body_literal: The description is assembled by the shell (`$(...)`, a variable, or backticks), so its sections could not be checked. Check the template sections yourself.
trigger.pre_pr.detail:
The pull-request check also found this:
{details}
trigger.pre_pr.settled_by: The outward guard asked about this call first. Answering it answers this check too.
trigger.pre_release.detected: Checking this release against the project workflow rules.
trigger.pre_release.reason:
This release breaks the project workflow rules.
{details}
trigger.pre_release.error.version: `{version}` is not a semantic version. Use `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally with a pre-release suffix such as `-rc.1`.
trigger.pre_release.error.version_mismat: The tag says `{tag}` but package.json says `{version}`. The tag and the published artefact must name the same version.
trigger.pre_release.error.prerelease_tag: `{version}` is a pre-release, so it must not be published to `latest`. Publish it with `--tag next`.
trigger.pre_release.error.changelog: The changelog has no `## [{section}]` section. Keep a Changelog keeps one at the top, and it is the section a release is cut from.
trigger.pre_release.warn.changelog_categ: `### {section}` is not a category this repository lists. Keep a Changelog lets a project group as it likes, so this is advice rather than a blocker — add the name to `releaseCheck.categories` if it belongs here.
trigger.pre_release.warn.tag_literal: The tag name is assembled by the shell (`$(...)`, a variable, or backticks), so only its literal text could be read. Check the resulting version yourself.
trigger.pre_release.warn.filter: This publishes another workspace package (`--filter {name}`), and its `package.json` could not be read, so the version was not checked against the tag. Point `--filter` at the package directory to have it read.
trigger.pre_release.warn.version_bump: `npm version {kind}` writes the manifest, commits and creates the tag in one step, so it passes no commit or tag check. Review the resulting commit and tag yourself.
trigger.pre_release.error.changelog_empt: The changelog has no entries for {version}. Write them under `[{section}]`, or move them into the `[{version}]` section when you cut the release.
trigger.pre_release.detail:
The release check also found this:
{details}
trigger.pre_release.settled_by: The other gate asked about this call first. Answering it answers this check too.
skill.summary: Project workflow conventions are available as a skill. Read it before committing, branching, or changing documentation.
